blinding_guess.why: The subscription that would carry /my_topic is created with a bare history depth (create_subscription(msg_class, topic, self.callback, 10), subscribers.py:108) and an explicit TODO that other QoS is unsupported (line 107). rosbridge_server therefore cannot adapt its reliability or durability to whatever publishes /my_topic; a best-effort or transient-local publisher would be QoS-incompatible and the bridge would silently forward nothing. The same file also mishandles late-joining clients on an already-subscribed topic: _new_sub_callback passes [self.new_subscriptions.values()] (a list holding a dict view) as the callback list (line 207), so the first message for the new client raises in the callback loop and is only logged (lines 187-193). Given that the packet singles out one consumed topic on a ROS 2 (foxy) revision, the fixed-QoS subscription path is the most plausible defect.

notes: rosbridge_server (ROS 2, ament_cmake, rclpy; package.xml:19-21) does not subscribe to any statically named topic. It delegates the 'subscribe' op to rosbridge_library (same repository snapshot, same version 1.0.2, exec_depend at rosbridge_server/package.xml:22; imported at scripts/rosbridge_websocket.py:56 and wired into RosbridgeProtocol at rosbridge_library/src/rosbridge_library/rosbridge_protocol.py:50). Topic name: supplied by the client at run time (subscribe.py:225), filtered by the topics_glob whitelist when that list is non-empty (subscribe.py:227-239; launch default topics_glob=''[*]''); topic:/my_topic does not appear anywhere in the snapshot, so it is in neither declares/not_declared nor references. msg_type: null because it is chosen at run time: the client's optional 'type' field (subscribe.py:249) or, if absent, the first type returned by node_handle.get_topic_names_and_types() for that topic (subscribers.py:75-90); a client-supplied type is normalised by ros_loader._splittype (accepts pkg/Type or pkg/msg/Type, ros_loader.py:193-204) and checked against the established type (subscribers.py:96-98). Hence definition_id is null (no definition to hash) and frame/units are null (the message type is unknown; rosbridge forwards the message as JSON/CBOR without interpreting frames). QoS: the code passes only an integer history depth of 10 to rclpy create_subscription (subscribers.py:108, and again for the temporary new-subscriber subscription at lines 150-151); reliability and durability are not set in code or configuration. Under rclpy an integer depth yields QoSProfile(depth=10) with the constructor's default reliability/durability (to my recollection SYSTEM_DEFAULT, resolved by the RMW to reliable/volatile for the Foxy default middleware); this recollection could not be verified from the sources allowed here (rclpy source is not a .msg/.srv/.action/.idl file), so both are recorded as null rather than cited. The QoS is fixed, not selected at run time from discovered publishers. rate_hz/min_rate_hz: not set; the client may request throttle_rate (ms) and queue_length per subscription, and the lowest across clients is applied (subscribe.py:94-95,179-180; subscription_modifiers.py:58 converts ms to s). Permissions: perm_grants records the client access-control gates (topics_glob/services_glob/params_glob whitelists and the authenticate flag); note that the authentication path imports nothing for Authentication (websocket_handler.py:36-37 commented out, 'TODO(@jubeira): Re-add once rosauth is ported to ROS2') yet uses Authentication at line 132, and websocket_handler.py:153 calls get_logger.error without parentheses. Other observations not tied to the element: scripts/rosbridge_tcp.py and rosbridge_udp.py still import rospy (ROS 1) and their handlers are not imported (src/rosbridge_server/__init__.py:5-7); scripts/rosbridge_websocket.py:306 calls node.destroy_node() on an undefined name 'node'; websocket.py:118-126 and client_mananger.py:44-52 both create a 'client_count' publisher with transient_local durability (provided elements, not in the packet). definition_hash.py was not run because no definition file applies.
